grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.rule: きのう、あけませんでした。きょう、あけます。

tables.caption: Whole polite forms: left column nonpast; middle column past affirmative; right column past negative
rows: うけとりませんでした

tables.caption: Source and recipient transfers; containers and placement

grammar.note_en:
A polite verb ending in ます is nonpast: it can describe an action now, a regular action, or a planned future action, depending on context. Polite past affirmative replaces the final ます with ました; polite past negative replaces it with ませんでした. Compare きのうはあけませんでした (“[He] did not open it yesterday”) with きょうはあけます (“[We] will open it today”). In きのうはかぎをうけとりませんでした / きょうはうけとります, Mei contrasts not receiving the key yesterday with her intention to receive it today. A negative says an action did not occur; it does not itself tell you why. The end of this chapter confirms the actual handover with うけとりました, “received.”

The ending does not change for a named person or an omitted subject. Speaker and context supply the people: the caretaker’s せんしゅう、かりました means “[I] borrowed [it] last week.” めいさんからかぎをかりました means “borrowed the key from Mei”; せんしゅう、わたしはかしました means “I lent it last week.” から names the source person with borrow/receive here, while に names the recipient with lend/hand over/return. This extends the already familiar endpoints into the explicitly shown transfer frames; it does not license arbitrary new verb patterns. Do not interchange かします, lend, かります, borrow, かえします, return a borrowed object, and かえります, return to a place.

The caretaker borrowed a reading-room book as well as Mei’s key last week. The book was returned yesterday; the key was not. The three books in the large shop parcel are a separate set, first opened today. The old room name on that parcel is a label; it is not evidence that the other parcel has the same sender, recipient or contents.

いれます takes the thing as を and its receiving container as に: かぎをかばんにいれます, “put the key into the bag.” おきます uses に for the place where something is set down: かぎはつくえのうえにおきました, “As for the key, [I] set it on the desk.” These are the two concrete frames shown here. They do not add a general dictionary-form or te-form paradigm. とどきました says something arrived; うけとりました says a person received it. A delivery can arrive at a place while the person who received it remains unknown.

きのう means yesterday; せんしゅう means last week. They locate the event without に in these examples. The date expressions じゅうににち and じゅうさんにち identify the 12th and 13th as complete readings. The paper is currently identified as yesterday’s delivery record; its printed date is じゅうににち. This avoids an untaught past noun predicate. Today’s quoted date is じゅうさんにち. Learn only these dated forms, not an invented rule for every day number.

そのあと means “after that” as a bounded sequencing expression. おちゃのあと means “after tea,” a familiar event expressed as a noun. The following そのあと links the next action to the immediately recalled event, without an untaught verb-modifying clause. General before/after clauses wait until chapter 17. まえ here is only the already taught まえのなまえ, the former name.

All story kanji retain authored furigana, including familiar characters. The new spatial kanji spell the known words うえ and した; the person character spells ひと. The two-character letter spelling represents the whole known word てがみ, not a lesson in guessing separate character meanings. Non-story examples and exercise answers remain kana.

The caretaker removes and keeps his private letter before offering the red outer envelope for the joint search; neither Mei nor Yui reads it. Mei finds the borrowed key in that envelope and receives it back. The two small invitations remain together in their separate envelope. The second delivery paper bears a different name and the current room destination; no second parcel is opened and no identity is inferred from its signature.

English reference for every form in the first table, in the same left-to-right order (nonpast; past affirmative; past negative): あけます — open/will open; あけました — opened; あけませんでした — did not open. うけとります — receive/will receive; うけとりました — received; うけとりませんでした — did not receive. かえします — return/will return a borrowed object; かえしました — returned it; かえしませんでした — did not return it. いれます — put/will put it in; いれました — put it in; いれませんでした — did not put it in. Each displayed form has already appeared in this story; the table is not an unshown full paradigm.

English reference for every row in the transfer/placement table: めいからかぎをかりました — “[I] borrowed the key from Mei.” めいにかぎをかえします — “[I] will return the key to Mei.” かばんにかぎをいれます — “[I] put/will put the key into the bag.” つくえのうえにかぎをおきました — “[I] set the key on the desk.” The table groups specific transfer, container and placement frames; its caption does not claim that every row describes a loan.

notes: Original contemporary Japanese narrative, entirely authored for the course; no authentic quotation or adapted passages. No audio. Four developed scenes with 40 workbook +8 A +8 B +6 C =62 responses.

The story places day3 on the fictional autumn13th and day2 on the12th, using only two explicitly dated whole forms. It retrospectively narrates the intervening day2 home delivery after chapter6’s actual stopping point; the earlier chapter is not claimed to have narrated it.

Three open-slot meanings are selected within the21-word ceiling: put into, set down and return a borrowed thing. Stable ja-07-03 まえ is recalled from6, never duplicated. Grammar, particles, register, morphology, readings, object custody and keys have been manually checked in the prescribed pass order; the independent review must adjudicate the questions below.

The first book parcel is opened only today and contains three shop books. It is separate from the book borrowed last week and returned yesterday, from the private letter/outer envelope and from the still-unlocated second parcel.

Every story Han occurrence has exact-source whole-word UTF-16 reading metadata. The five newly allocated characters are 上下人手紙; no character meaning licenses another lexical sense. Four earlier entries receive only dated script forms and earlier kana card stages stay intact.

Non-story learner fields remain kana. English semantic cues distinguish new miniature exercise incidents; no tested answer is supplied in Japanese. Only C allows open sentences and its stages are visible in the instruction. Banks have same-class extras for noun and time-expression answers; accepted closed alternatives were checked against the stated English cues.

Parent preflight corrects three tense-specific card anchors and the word order that produced a spuriousにち match; actual whole date occurrences are counted separately from overlaps. Only the caretaker inspects his own bag; the empty outer envelope is explicitly offered, and he retrieves his own letter before closing it in the envelope. Each bag’s owner is named. The address belongs to an institution rather than equalling its name. No new meaning, deadline or numeric series is added.

Parent design disposition: adopt the explicitly dated G07 polite past/negative forms, bounded transfer/arrival/placement frames and the two taught whole calendar labels. Sequence expressions are limited toそのあと andおちゃのあと here; there is no past-copula/adjective, plain, te-form, general demonstrative or before/after-clause licence. Calendar metadata is aligned with published5/6 and the fixed13th gathering. The small box and sealed large parcel remain distinct.

Review1105-003004-1823 repairs: motion uses taughtへ; the return cue does not say home; the second record’s address and personal-name fields are separately identified. Uniform attested-form columns and explicit English references translate every table example. Reallocated remembered actions now connect the letter, adjacent key and envelope rather than adding volume. Past card backs and delivery referent are explicit.

Ready/ready recheck1105-004642-17511 resolves all blockers. The minor letter label now clears the desk leg. Final2617atoms against2480,62responses,107ruby spans; all four reading stages and custody/inference changes remain. No target is recalibrated and no extra scene is added.
